basis.corpus_label: static hypothetical selected facts, no live deployment
basis.source: Only the public supported reference profile supplied in this independent session.
basis.inventory_semantics: Every runtime JSON is independently authored synthetic selected facts, a hypothesis rather than a real observation. Normal inventories mirror declared bind entries without bind options; the two explicit mismatch cases are documented in their reasons.

hypotheses.image_code_correspondence: The shared hypothetical image identifies known code by stipulation, not measurement.
hypotheses.egress: Only the network declaration is analyzed; no live external egress claim is assessed.

label_meanings.SAFE_IN_SUPPORTED_MODEL: Matches the supplied supported model under its given hypotheses; no live safety claim.
label_meanings.REFUTED_CONFIGURATION: Explicit contradiction of the supplied principal, environment, mount, network or selected-inventory correspondence policy.
label_meanings.UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION: Unsupported declaration prevents assurance within the selected model.

basis.checksum_paths: SHA256SUMS paths are relative to corpus/.

cases.reason: The six principals, selected fields, private writer mounts and isolated network match the given supported model; receiver omits its optional channel mount.
Receiver includes the explicitly optional read-write channel mount; all other authority remains within the given profile.
All four read-only channel consumers use the explicitly permitted bind.selinux=z option; it does not change declared read-only authority.
Broker and receiver private bind entries use the permitted selinux=z option while retaining the required source, target and writer permissions.
Receiver has its optional channel mount and every bind uses the allowed selinux=z annotation; all required principals and mount permissions still follow the profile.
Agent-a explicitly runs as UID 0 instead of UID 23701, granting excess identity authority and contradicting the principal policy.
Agent-b uses agent-a's UID 23701 instead of its distinct UID 23702, collapsing the two required agent principals.
Reviewer has a read-write channel bind although its only permitted bind is read-only; the declaration grants an unauthorized writer path.
Approver receives a writable sink bind in addition to its channel reader bind, exposing the receiver-only output writer path.
Broker receives a writable sink bind, exceeding its permitted channel and database writer mounts.
Receiver's required sink writer bind is read-only, contradicting the supported output configuration. This is a functional profile violation, without an assertion of an exploit.
Receiver's /output writer bind points at the channel directory instead of the configured sink source; the required source-to-target correspondence is false.
An unlisted synthetic credential environment key is supplied to broker. Credentials and extra environment names violate the explicit supported policy; the value is a dummy marker.
Reviewer declares the approver role while retaining reviewer UID and environment identity, creating contradictory principal declarations.
The sole declared network has internal=false instead of the required internal=true. This refutes the declaration profile without asserting measured external reachability.
Compose retains agent-a UID 23701 but the synthetic selected inventory states UID 23700. The paired hypotheses contradict explicit principal correspondence.
The synthetic approver inventory adds a writable database mount absent from Compose. The pair contradicts selected mount correspondence and introduces unauthorized hypothetical writer authority.
A restart declaration is outside the six supported service fields. Its presence requires UNKNOWN even though selected inventory facts match the supported baseline.
Service labels are an unlisted Compose feature. The harmless synthetic label cannot be treated as supported assurance.
Deploy resource limits are outside the selected service-field model; their effect is not represented by the inventory.
Service-level read_only is outside the supported field set, even when it appears restrictive; selected mount facts do not justify assurance for that declaration.
An additional tmpfs declaration is not an allowed long-form bind and is outside the selected authority model. No assertion about its live effect is made.
Service network membership is declared as an object rather than the required networks=[isolated] list. The alternative Compose form is unsupported despite the same selected network name.
Agent-b uses the Compose list form for environment rather than the required object. The represented key names agree, but this representation is outside the supported interface.
A bind.propagation option is supplied in addition to the allowed bind.selinux=z. This unmodelled bind option requires UNKNOWN; selected inventory deliberately omits the bind option object.
